name: Desko
tagline: Use your old smartphone as a desk widget for your PC
description: Desko turns a spare phone into an always-on desk dashboard: a single lightweight Python process runs on your PC, collects things worth looking at, and pushes them over a WebSocket to one browser tab on the phone sitting on your desk stand. No app to install, no account, no cloud, no build tooling — you open a URL and it just runs. The display cycles through five scenes: an idle clock with weather and phone battery, a music scene with album art and time-synced karaoke lyrics, a stats scene with CPU/GPU load and sparklines, a dev scene with git status and live VS Code state, and a server-side Pomodoro timer. Everything degrades gracefully — no media playing, no LibreHardwareMonitor, and the widgets just hide. The frontend is vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with no build step, designed to run on old budget phones with under 1% idle CPU and a performance mode for weak GPUs.
highlights: Repurposes an old phone into a live desk-widget panel over WiFi
Five scenes: idle clock, music with synced karaoke lyrics, stats, git/dev, Pomodoro
Single Python process with WebSocket diffs — no app install, no cloud, no build step
Everything degrades gracefully: missing sources hide, nothing shows a dead dash
Performance mode and vanilla frontend tuned for old budget phones
curatorNote: Polished e-waste reuse — repurposes an aging phone into a live desk-widget panel, 148 stars days after launch. The karaoke-lyrics music scene and the graceful-degradation discipline make it feel far more mature than its age.
